claim_verdicts.evidence: "By default, a pod is non-isolated for ingress; all inbound connections are allowed." and "By default, if no policies exist in a namespace, then all ingress and egress traffic is allowed to and from pods in that namespace." Execution: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/network-policy.txt line 4, from security-lessons: "db.donhang.svc.cluster.local:5432 - accepting connections".

Namespaces page: "Namespaces provide a scope for names. Names of resources need to be unique within a namespace, but not across namespaces." Network Policies page: "By default, a pod is non-isolated for ingress; all inbound connections are allowed." — no namespace condition; isolation arises only from a NetworkPolicy selecting the Pod. Execution (network-policy.txt line 4) shows a cross-namespace connection accepted.

"A pod is isolated for ingress if there is any NetworkPolicy that both selects the pod and has \"Ingress\" in its policyTypes ... When a pod is isolated for ingress, the only allowed connections into the pod are those from the pod's node and those allowed by the ingress list of some NetworkPolicy that applies to the pod for ingress. Reply traffic for those allowed connections will also be implicitly allowed."

"Network policies do not conflict; they are additive. If any policy or policies apply to a given pod for a given direction, the connections allowed in that direction from that pod is the union of what the applicable policies allow. Thus, order of evaluation does not affect the policy result."

"Network policies are implemented by the network plugin. To use network policies, you must be using a networking solution which supports NetworkPolicy. Creating a NetworkPolicy resource without a controller that implements it will have no effect." and "POSTing this to the API server for your cluster will have no effect unless your chosen networking solution supports network policy."

kind docs (WebFetch) say only "KIND ships with a simple networking implementation (kindnetd)"; nothing on NetworkPolicy. Execution evidence: deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/main.tf keeps the default CNI (no disable_default_cni), and network-policy.txt shows the same pg_isready go from 'accepting connections' (line 4) to 'no response' (line 19) once the policies sync. Verified by run on donhang-staging, not by kind docs. git show at the tag was not permitted; working tree + captured output used.

Printed words 'accepting connections' / 'no response' and 'exit code 2' seen in network-policy.txt lines 4, 19-20. No drop-vs-refuse inference remains in lesson or quiz (grep 'drop|refus|packet').

"the only allowed connections into the pod are those from the pod's node and those allowed by the ingress list"; hostNetwork section: "since hostNetwork pods have the same IP addresses as the nodes they reside on, their connections will be treated as node connections" (implying pod-network Pods are not). Execution: staging has workers = 0 (single node), so probe in security-lessons shares db's node yet gets 'no response'; 'Pods in donhang not ready: 0'.

"An empty podSelector selects all pods in the namespace." and "You can create a 'default' ingress isolation policy for a namespace by creating a NetworkPolicy that selects all pods but does not allow any ingress traffic to those pods. ... This ensures that even pods that aren't selected by any other NetworkPolicy will still be isolated for ingress."

"podSelector: This selects particular Pods in the same namespace as the NetworkPolicy which should be allowed as ingress sources"; "namespaceSelector: This selects particular namespaces for which all Pods should be allowed as ingress sources"; "Each rule allows traffic which matches both the from and ports sections."
